day_shape: CENTCOM's Project Freedom escort operation runs through the Strait of Hormuz with six Iranian small boats destroyed and a Maersk US-flagged transit, Iranian drones wound three Indians at Fujairah, US intel assesses limited new damage to Iran's nuclear programme, and UN OCHA revises Iran emergency strategy nationwide.

threads.label: Project Freedom escorts in Strait of Hormuz
threads.summary: CENTCOM said US forces destroyed six Iranian small boats, intercepted cruise missiles and drones, and escorted a Maersk US-flagged ship through the Strait, with 50 commercial vessels redirected under the Iran blockade. Adm. Brad Cooper detailed the operation involving USS Abraham Lincoln, USS Tripoli, USS Pinckney and over 100 aircraft; CENTCOM denied Iranian state media claims that an IRGC missile struck a US warship.

threads.label: Regime claims Hormuz under Iranian control
threads.summary: IRIB and Defa Press said the Strait of Hormuz remains entirely under Iran's control and described Project Freedom as failed, with Speaker Ghalibaf claiming a 'new equation' for the waterway. IRIB also reported a US KC-135R tanker over the Persian Gulf transmitting emergency code 7700, and the IRGC navy issued a new map of areas it claims to control.

threads.label: Iran strikes UAE, Pezeshkian-IRGC rift
threads.summary: Three Indian citizens were moderately wounded in an Iranian drone attack on Fujairah's oil complex, with Iran International reporting Pezeshkian branded the IRGC escalation 'madness'. Abu Dhabi's crisis centre warned of hundreds of thousands of cyber attacks originating from Iran, and the Jerusalem Post reported no change to Israeli home-front rules.

threads.label: US intel: limited new damage to nuclear programme
threads.summary: US intelligence agencies assess that recent military action caused only limited additional damage to Iran's nuclear programme, leaving the weapons timeline largely unchanged from June. The Jerusalem Post reported the timeline was set back by about a year and remains static, and cited Trump weighing punishment against further entanglement.

threads.label: South Lebanon exchanges continue
threads.summary: The IDF said Hezbollah fired twice at troops in southern Lebanon overnight without injuries and struck a structure after an anti-tank missile launch, while also dismantling a 30-metre tunnel and around 15 infrastructure sites. Defa Press relayed Hezbollah's claim of operations against Israeli vehicles and soldiers, and Lebanon's parliament speaker ruled out talks with Israel until the war ends.

threads.label: UK-linked Iran cases and Golders Green attack
threads.summary: Times of Israel and Jerusalem Post reported Iranian-British Ashkan Asadian chased the perpetrator of last week's Golders Green stabbing, and two people were arrested over an arson attack on a memorial wall for Iranian protesters. Iran International said British couple Lindsay and Craig Foreman, jailed 10 years on espionage charges, have been barred from visiting each other in Evin for three weeks.

threads.label: Iran humanitarian and domestic toll
threads.summary: UN OCHA's ReliefWeb published a revised operational strategy for Iran citing nationwide complex emergency and continued escalation of hostilities, while Iran International reported Tehran media breaking silence on the war's livelihood toll and the secret burial of executed Iranian-Swedish citizen Kourosh Keyvani. Defa Press claimed 630,000 people entered Iran during the Ramadan war days, and IRIB reported an 18% drop in Nowruz passenger transport.
